steps.message:
This one is rung 1 on the skills ladder — a session lifetime is security posture, not just a value — so I'm stopping before the edit rather than after it.

The change would be `config.js:3`, `SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES: 30` → `480`.

The consequence: a stolen or abandoned session stays valid 16× longer. An unattended laptop, a leaked session cookie, or a token lifted from a shared machine currently becomes useless after 30 idle minutes; at 8 hours it survives a full workday. `server.js:3` confirms this value is the sole expiry control here — there's no idle-timeout or re-auth layer behind it to limit the blast radius.

That may well be the right tradeoff (it usually is when people are being logged out mid-task), but it's your call to make, not mine to assume. Confirm and I'll make the one-line change.

One thing worth knowing before you decide: 8 hours of *absolute* lifetime plus a short idle timeout gets you the "stop logging me out" benefit without the stolen-cookie exposure. That's a bigger change than a one-liner, so I haven't gone there — just flagging it exists.
hmm, good point — ok, make it 2 hours instead
